title: Action request buffer model
summary: Button presses are latched by the engine and used when the current animation lets that action run. The latch has no timer; it only clears when the engine says so.
values: 33 action bits (HKS ACTION_ARM_*). Per frame: pressed = held & ~prevHeld; pending |= pressed & acceptMask (+0xd0); requested (+0x30, env 1106) |= pending & executeMask (+0xe0). Masks are rebuilt every frame and zeroed at the end of the update. Per-action hold timers at +0xe8 (env 1108).
how: SprjChrActionRequestModule (RTTI vtable 0x142a729d8), update FUN_140b2c190; setters FUN_140b2be00 (accept), FUN_140b2bdc0 (execute).
check: Mash attack before the swing opens its accept window: the presses are dropped; a press inside the window chains.

title: Accept flags (what a press latches)
summary: A TAE ChrActionFlag opens a window in which a press of a given action is remembered.
values: Accept ids: 87 all actions, 1 attack, 9/150 guard, 25 step, 151 jump, 30 item, 136 prosthetic tool. Bits: 0 attack, 1 sub (tool), 2 guard, 4 jump, 5/13/14 step, 7 item, 18 shinobi tool. Example: tap slash buffers from frame 6, Combo1 hold from frame 21; guard, jump and step get early windows (frames 3-15).
how: TAE dispatcher FUN_140b59170 case 0 ChrActionFlag -> FUN_140b51b70 (a u16 id switch, gated by an SpEffect check on arg[7]).
check: Record a press at frame 5 and frame 7 of Combo1: only the second is remembered.
note: Animations without any action flags (idle, locomotion loops) accept and execute everything.

title: Execute flags (when a remembered press fires)
summary: A second set of ChrActionFlags opens the cancel window in which a remembered press actually starts the action.
values: Execute ids: 4 and 115 attack, 116 sub attack, 16 and 117 guard, 26 step, 119 jump, 31 item, 137 tool. The flags the player code gated on before were the execute ones.
how: Same dispatcher; execute mask +0xe0 via FUN_140b2bdc0.
check: Attack twice quickly: the second slash starts at the cancel frame (about 15 for the tap slash).

title: Which transitions clear the buffer
summary: Most transitions clear every remembered press. Locomotion, quick turns, falls and landings keep them.
values: HKS FireEvent calls ResetRequest -> act(9101) -> FUN_140b2afd0 (+0x188 bit 0), dropping all pending presses; FireEventNoReset keeps them. FireEvent used 891 times, FireEventNoReset 203 times in the player set.
check: Press jump during a hit reaction, then recover: jump is not performed after the reaction.
note: Pending is also cleared when combat puts the player in a damage state.

title: Buffered input fires one game frame late
summary: A remembered press fires about one TAE frame (two game frames) after the cancel flag starts, because the script sees the flags set by the previous update.
values: Live: attack flag 115: 16.0 vs flag at 15, 9.9 vs 9, 13 vs 12, 19 vs 18; guard flag 117: about 7.0 vs 6. A fresh press makes the anim change in about 1 game frame.
how: HKS reads env flags from the previous frame TAE update.
check: Time a buffered slash against the execute flag in the TAE view.

title: Guard must still be held when the press fires
summary: A tapped guard that was let go before its window opened is dropped. Attack presses survive release.
values: Exceptions that keep released guard taps: the deflect spam chain (ref 212, StandToDeflectGuard*) and the additive deflect (ref 228) with guard cancel 412 (f9, e.g. StandDeflectHardSmall: press f1.5, release f4 gives StandToDeflectGuard at f9.5).
how: HKS env 1108 duration check on guard plus TAE refs.
check: Tap and release guard during a slash recovery before the guard window: no guard.

title: Hold and release on attacks
summary: Releasing the attack button before a TAE window opens triggers a release slash at that window.
values: Release before ref 208 starts Release at TAE frame 6.0-6.5 (matches the 208 window at f6).
check: Tap attack and let go before frame 6: Release slash starts at frame 6.

title: Additive action input (buffer for the next move)
summary: Certain moves open "add action input" windows in which a button press is stored in a separate layer and replayed when the cancel window comes. Each action has an enable and a cancel SpEffect ref.
values: Refs (enable/cancel): jump 403/404, use item 405/406, crouch 407/408, attack 409/410, guard 411/412, sub attack 413/414, wire 415/416, wall hang 417/418, kick(dodge) 419/420, sub weapon change 421/422, resend 423, wall jump 425, special attack 429/430. HKS BEH_A_ADD_ACTION_INPUT_* fire on env(1106, ...) of the matching arm. Clip example AddActionInputWireShoot a000_299026 (0.4 s).

ours.where: fireguy-rustsekiro/src/player.rs (wire, jump, kick, crouch; no additive layer)

check: Press jump while the previous state is still in a jump-cancel window and see AddActionInputJump play.
note: Ours plays no additive layers anywhere, so some presses are dropped (grapple notes).

title: Hold time of a button
summary: Several actions depend on how long a button has been held, not just pressed. env 1108 returns the hold time in milliseconds.
values: Used: sprint if SP_MOVE > 0; step by press-hold with ENABLE_PRESS_STEP and > 0; swamp run if SP_MOVE > 200; air hang grab with the hang button held > 0; env 333 is the frame time in ms.
check: Hold dodge 0.1 s vs 0.3 s in a swamp.

title: Dodge button: tap steps, hold sprints
summary: The same button gives a step on press and a sprint on hold, depending on the state.
values: BEH_A_GROUND_STEP uses env(1106) (press) or buffered kick input or ENABLE_PRESS_STEP with env(1108) > 0; BEH_A_SPRINT uses env(1108) > 0 with the TAE sprint-transition or running states; no sprint or step in waterside. PRM_RUN_STICK values apply to walk/run only.
check: Tap Shift while running (step) and hold it (sprint).

title: Action arms (input channels)
summary: The script talks to 18 input channels called action arms, each tied to a game action.
values: ACTION_ARM_ATTACK 0, SUB_ATTACK 1, GUARD 2, WIRE_SHOOT 3, JUMP 4, SP_MOVE 5 (dodge/sprint), USE_ITEM 7, CHANGE_WEAPON_L 10, WALL_HANG 12, BACKSTEP 13, ROLLING 14, CROUCH 15, SHINOBI_WEP_ACTION 18, SWIM_ACCELERATION 28, SWIM_UP 29, SWIM_DOWN 30, EAVESDROP 31, SPECIAL_ATTACK 32. env 1106 is used at 142 sites with 18 distinct arms.
check: List the arms in the sim input.

title: Default key and pad bindings
summary: DefaultKeyAssignParam rows bind each game action to a keyboard code, mouse button and pad button. Keyboard ids are DirectInput scan code plus 69.
values: DefaultKeyAssignParam00 (5 presets): move W/S/A/D = 86/100/99/101 with pad 3003/3003/3002/3002 (stick axes); action 5 step/sprint kb 111 (Shift) pad 2005; 6 jump kb 126 (Space) pad 2004; 7 crouch kb 85 (Q) pad 2010; 20 interact/hug/hang kb 87 (E) pad 2006; 21 use item kb 88 (R) pad 2000; 19 grapple kb 102 (F) pad 3000; mouse ids 1/2/8 = right/left/middle. Pad 2000-2003 are the d-pad.
check: Reset keybinds and compare with the table; note pad ids are mapped to buttons by the exe, not in the param.
note: Pad ids 2006-2013 are not decoded to button names.

title: Stick and camera-relative movement vector
summary: Movement input is the left stick turned by the camera yaw. Its length is the stick level; walking halves it and releasing zeros it.
values: ChrManipulator (PadManipulator for Wolf) +0xc0 = move stick (-x, 0, -y) rotated by camera yaw, unnormalised, halved on walk (FUN_1407f0f50); +0x80 right stick (camera), +0xd0 mouse. HKS reads MoveSpeedLevel, MoveAngle (locked) and TurnAngle (free).
check: Push the stick at 50 percent while walking: MoveSpeedLevel is about 0.5.

title: World action prompts (ActionButtonParam)
summary: Prompts for talking, opening, picking up and similar actions appear when Wolf is within a small cylinder in front of the spot. Each row has size, angle and a 3 s lockout after use.
values: ActionButtonParam 305 rows. Defaults: radius 1.5 m, height 1.0, baseHeightOffset -0.25, angle 180, priority 10, execInvalidTime 3.0 s. Pickup/gesture rows 3000/3010: radius 2.0, height 4.0, offset -2.0, gameKey 1. Object rows 4200-4220: radius 2-3 m, raycastType 1. Sliding rows 5000/5010: angle 90, allowAngle 45, dummypoly 195/194, height 0.5.
how: Map ActionButton regions + ObjAct; menu text ids in textId.
